response.sql: WITH team_avg AS (SELECT team_id, AVG(w) AS avg_wins, AVG((g - l) * 1.0 / NULLIF(l, 0)) AS avg_g_minus_l_ratio FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS mean_avg_wins FROM team_avg) SELECT t.team_id, t.avg_wins, t.avg_g_minus_l_ratio, t.avg_wins - o.mean_avg_wins AS gap_above_mean FROM team_avg t CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE t.avg_wins > o.mean_avg_wins ORDER BY gap_above_mean DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each manager_half row is one record, so AVG(w) per team_id averages over its rows. The mean of all teams' average wins is the unweighted mean of the per-team averages, not a pooled mean over all rows.
Rows with l = 0 give a missing ratio (NULLIF avoids division by zero), and AVG ignores those rows. The ratio uses 1.0 multiplication to avoid integer division.
